drugs.name: Doxycycline (tetracyclines)
drugs.mechanism: Binds the 30S subunit and blocks aminoacyl-tRNA attachment, so the peptide chain cannot elongate; bacteriostatic; binds divalent and trivalent cations
drugs.adverseEffects: Binds calcium in growing bone and teeth: irreversible tooth staining and effects on growth, so not used in pregnancy or young children
drugs.use: Q fever; Mycoplasma pneumonia (no cell wall, so beta-lactams fail); outpatient CAP in a patient without comorbidities

drugs.name: Metronidazole
drugs.mechanism: Nitroimidazole prodrug reduced inside anaerobic organisms to nitrogen free radicals that damage DNA
drugs.use: Anaerobic coverage, paired with a beta-lactam, for aspiration pneumonia; second line for C. difficile colitis after oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin

drugs.name: Amphotericin B
drugs.mechanism: IV polyene that binds ergosterol, the sterol fungal membranes use in place of cholesterol, disrupting the membrane; Candida lusitaniae and C. guilliermondii can resist it
drugs.adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity, additive with aminoglycosides and cisplatin; low selective toxicity because fungal and human cells are both eukaryotic, so side effects are common
drugs.use: Severe or disseminated endemic mycoses; induction for talaromycosis; with flucytosine for cryptococcal meningitis; with debridement for mucormycosis; disseminated candidiasis

drugs.name: Fluconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole that blocks fungal ergosterol synthesis and reaches the CSF; heavy use has selected Candida krusei (intrinsically resistant) and C. glabrata (reduced susceptibility)
drugs.use: Mild or persistent pulmonary coccidioidomycosis and coccidioidal meningitis; long-term suppression of cryptococcal meningitis in AIDS and mild cryptococcal lung disease

drugs.name: Itraconazole
drugs.mechanism: Oral azole: inhibits synthesis of ergosterol, the fungal membrane sterol
drugs.use: Oral first-line for mild-moderate histoplasmosis, blastomycosis and paracoccidioidomycosis; oral maintenance after amphotericin induction for talaromycosis

drugs.name: Voriconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole antifungal: blocks fungal ergosterol synthesis
drugs.use: Drug of choice for invasive aspergillosis; posaconazole, caspofungin or amphotericin B are second line
